en: The Sevenfold Supreme Praise:
Homage to the Glorious Lokanātha! [I bow to him] who has Amitābha upon his crown and eyes as broad as lotus petals.

I bow my head in salutation to that Lord of the World, who destroys all misfortune, who has rendered delusion, illusion, and evil powerless, who holds a golden lotus in his hand, and who alone is truly skilled among the world-protectors. || 1 ||
The jewel-encrusted crown, which possesses the splendor of Aruṇa and Varuṇa, which is the cause of awakening-consciousness at the Bodhi tree, which is a bridge across the ocean of saṃsāra,
which has brought about the destruction of the god of love, and which is the banner of the Bodhisattvas and others.
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World. || 2 ||
Dwelling within the lotus, having cast far away the noose of Kandarpa,
the refuge of gods, humans, and demons, possessing the radiance of the full moon,
the delight of virtuous people, and shining with the brilliance of ten million suns—
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World.
Upon whose chest the Naga is placed, who has released all passion, who is the division of the ocean of existence, the sole path to the bliss of liberation,
whose limbs are like refined gold, and who possesses the singular passion for the awakening to enlightenment—
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World.
The king of the sons of the supreme Jina, resplendent with a garland of liberation,
possessing a most graceful royal serpent, beautiful with scattered rays of light;
the king of joyful hosts, who protects the king of the immortals.
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World. || 5 ||
He who assumed the form of a honeybee, who is the well that quenches the thirst of hunger, who took the form of a horse for the sake of good conduct, who subdued the king of Siṃhala,
who is the fragrant incense of aguru, and who has maintained all forms.
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World.
This daily recitation, which removes my threefold committed sins and the three-fold torments, is a lament within the circle of the gods;
it is a bundle of fear for hell and a bow of ignorance that causes division.
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World.

Through his own devotion, he attained a multitude of excellent virtues— those people who had performed auspicious deeds, were striving for liberation from suffering, whose impurities had dissolved, and who delighted in worship with devotion.
With my head bowed in prostration, I praise that Lord of the World.
I celebrate the awakening of the Buddha, the accomplishment achieved through the ten powers,
for those terrified by birth and death who have been led into the snares of Māra,
whose minds are of defiled conduct and whose wealth is filled with ignorance.
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World. || 9 ||
I take refuge here for a moment in the most excellent jewel of the Sugata, the Dharmakāya together with the Saṃgha, who have brought about the destruction of the limbs of Māra;
with a joyful mind, they have attained the singular effort for the acquisition of awakening.
With my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to that Lord of the World. || 10 ||
This work, composed by Pīyūṣananda out of devotion for the lotus feet of Śrī Lokanātha, is not overly extensive yet rich in content;
it is endowed with the sevenfold worship and is both flavorful and exceedingly charming.
It indeed immediately creates the path for proceeding to the realm of Saukhyāvatī. || 11 ||
By whatever merit has been acquired through praising this Lord of Sages, the Teacher of the World, who bestows the accomplishment of all aims— may that merit lead one to the realm of Saugatyavatī,
which arises from the singular joy of the blossoming nectar of the lotus feet of Śrī Lokeśvara.
Having conquered the supreme Sudurjaya, who removes the afflictions of the world, he is liberated and stainless.
The Sevenfold Unsurpassed Praise of the Glorious Noble Avalokiteśvara is complete.
